Getting started

What it takes from your side, what you get, and what comes after.

Your timeThree meetings, about three hours in total: a kickoff with you, a screen-share of your tools with whoever built them, and a final review. If they can't make it, the screen-share moves inside the two weeks, or a teammate walks me through it.
What I needA few docs, what you pay to run the tools, the inputs your criteria uses for adobo, and total sales numbers if it has shipped.
Your dataTotal sales, not customer-level records. I don't take a copy of customer data, and anything that comes up on the screen-share stays on your screen. Both sides sign an NDA first.
What you getOne page: where you are on the build, what's least efficient, which hypotheses aren't holding up, and what to stop. Plus three next steps, each with a number for success and a date to check it, and a pressure test of one plan: how each person who signs off would argue against it, and what still holds up. I go deep on the two areas you pick at kickoff and give the rest a first pass, marked as first pass. Anything I'm unsure about is marked as unsure, and if you disagree with a finding, your pushback goes on the page at the final review. All of it is yours.
Payment$5,000 fixed. Half at kickoff, half at the final review. You can stop anytime and keep everything.
AfterNothing, unless you want help with a next step. Each is priced on its own, and the $5,000 is credited toward the first. Each step has its own check date, and your team can run that check; what it shows makes the next step sharper, whoever runs it.
Next steps I can take on
  • Rules for your AI tools: what they always do, what needs a check first, what they never do.
  • A small test your team can rerun: past decisions with known outcomes that the tools have to get right.
  • Pulling every number a partner contract commits to, tied to its clause, next to what the partner actually delivered. The gaps are findings to review with whoever owns the deal, not legal or financial advice. New for contracts, and run without sending the text to an outside model.

The full checklist

The five results you said you expect, plus two I'd add. In two weeks I go deep on the two you pick at kickoff and give the rest a first pass, marked as first pass.

  1. 01Accuracy. Where the data warehouse, the MCP environment and your foundational datasets meet the outside world, and which outputs get trusted without anyone checking them.
  2. 02Efficiency. Steps that are still done by hand, or automated when they don't need to be.
  3. 03Speed. How long it takes to get from a question to a decision you can act on.
  4. 04Cost savings. Whether moving it on-prem would actually be cheaper, and what you pay for but don't use.
  5. 05One source of truth. Whether it builds on one record, or grows data bloat and tech debt.
  6. 06What reaches an AI model. Where data goes, as your builders walk me through it: which customer data, personal details and partner terms reach an AI model or an outside service, and whether they need to.
  7. 07Facts or estimates. Which numbers are hard facts and which are estimates (customer simulations, trend calls, partner-risk warnings), whether each estimate says how sure it is, and whether anyone checks it against what actually happened.
